prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (max 500 words)

Core values and priorities
- Freedom, Justice, Honesty; green principles across all policy.
- Invest in schools, hospitals, police; raise pensions; free personal care for the elderly.
- Empower professionals; cut central bureaucracy; protect civil liberties.

Health
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals; add 10,000 beds; £1,000 average pay rise for lowest-paid NHS staff.
- More prevention and diagnostics; restore free dental and eye checks; expand scanning.
- End charges for long-term personal care; create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end the “postcode lottery” and drive drug prices down; aim to scrap prescription charges over time.
- Patient Care Guarantees; no-fault compensation; end mixed-sex wards; ban age discrimination; decentralise NHS management.

Education, skills and jobs
- Extra £3bn a year for education, funded by 1p on income tax.
- Primary class sizes averaged to 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants; paid prep time; training salaries; more ICT/books; scrap performance-related pay and reduce testing (no SATs at 7).
- Replace National Curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; cut bureaucracy; reform Ofsted.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorest; raise loan repayment threshold.
- Entitlement to publicly funded learning up to Level 2/3; simplify funding; expand lifelong learning.
- Replace the New Deal with a Flexible Guarantee via a combined Benefits and Jobs Agency; training incentives for SMEs; paid study leave for 16–24s.

Law and order
- 6,000 more police; 2,000 part-time community officers; Community Safety Force for low-level disorder.
- Independent police complaints system; focus on crime prevention; rehabilitation and work/education in prisons; more community sentences.
- Strengthen victims’ rights; hate crime units; keep jury trial; end most mandatory sentencing.

Transport
- Free off-peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim half-fares for under-19s.
- Abolish VED for the greenest vehicles; increase it for the most polluting; no real-terms fuel duty rise.
- Give councils powers for congestion charging/bonds; double rail freight by 2010.
- Stronger public control: create a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure Railtrack toward not-for-profit; bond-financed, not-for-profit Tube; prioritise road maintenance; tighter aviation controls; not-for-profit NATS.

Pensions, wages and benefits
- Raise basic state pension (larger boosts for over-75/80); fund via 50% tax rate on income over £100k; Independent Pensions Authority.
- Move toward a citizen’s pension and second-pillar accounts.
- Annual minimum wage review; same rate for 16+; cut taxes for the low paid over time; extra support for disabled people and long-term poor families; replace CSA with family courts.

Business, consumers and environment
- Cut red tape; £1,500 Business Rates Allowance for small firms; boost R&D; carbon tax to replace Climate Change Levy; 10% renewables by 2010; phase out nuclear over time.
- Toughen competition law; stronger bank regulation (e.g., ATM charges); enhance employee rights and HSE powers.

Democracy, rights, and communities
- Electoral reform: AV+ referendum for Westminster; STV for local/EU; votes at 16; elected Senate; stronger FOI; Equality Act and Equality Commission; repeal Section 28.
- Devolution to nations/regions; replace Council Tax with local income tax.
- Recycling (60% in 10 years), brownfield-first planning, flood task force, GM moratorium to 2004; CAP/CFP reform; Ministry for Rural Affairs; more affordable housing.

Europe, foreign policy and defence
- Pro-EU reformer: enlargement; EU constitution; more transparency; UK veto kept in key areas; stronger CFSP; ECB transparency.
- Enable euro entry after a referendum at a sustainable rate.
- Human-rights-led foreign policy; end arms export subsidies; support ICC/UN reform and peacekeeping; maintain defence spending and minimal nuclear deterrent; oppose US NMD.
